visitInfo.title: Finding the studio
visitInfo.intro: First floor, in a yard off Green Street, six minutes' walk from Upton Park.

steps: Leave the station and turn left onto Green Street
Plashet Yard is through the arch on the right; the studio is up the stairs
Walk through the arch into the yard

parking.name: Pay-by-phone bays on the side streets
parking.price: check the signs on the street
parking.note: Most nearby streets are residents only; read the signs.

access.label: A changing room with a curtain and a mirror

visitInfo.accessNote: The studio is up one flight of stairs. If stairs are hard for you, tell us and we'll bring the pieces down to the ground-floor room.
visitInfo.payment: Card, Apple Pay or bank transfer.

questions.a: Measure from the top of your shoulder to the floor and use the hem line above, or the chart by height. Tell us your shoes: heels need a longer length.

questions.q: Do the abayas come in sizes as well as lengths?
questions.a: Our abayas are cut loose, one width to a UK 18; the length is what changes. Above a UK 18, ask us about made to measure.
Our last order dates are above, counted from the first day Eid may fall. After that, collect from the studio.
Unworn pieces with their tags can be returned within 14 days of delivery. Made-to-measure pieces can't, because they're made for you.

questions.q: Can I try things on with my family?
questions.a: Yes: request a private appointment for up to five of you. The studio is women only during appointments.
Cool hand wash or a gentle cycle in a bag, hung to dry, pressed on the reverse on a low heat.

pages.title: Our story
pages.description: Why Taroub makes abayas in five lengths, from a studio in east London.
pages.intro: Taroub began with one problem: abayas that pooled on the floor, or stopped at the ankle.

blocks.heading: Five lengths
blocks.body:
Every abaya here is cut in five lengths, two inches apart, so it stops just above the floor in the shoes you wear. We'd rather you measured once than returned twice.

We make in small runs, in satin, crepe and organza, and keep the pieces in the studio, where you can try them with your family.
